short: A priced offer sent before the work or supply happens.
seoTitle: Quotation — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A quotation is a formal priced offer sent to a customer before a sale, setting out items, quantities, rates, taxes, validity and terms.
definition: A quotation is a formal priced offer sent to a customer before a sale, setting out items, quantities, rates, taxes, validity and terms. Accepted, it becomes the basis for the order and the eventual invoice.
bodyHtml:
Why Quotation matters

Most billing disputes start in the quotation — an unstated tax basis, an open-ended validity, or a scope line loose enough to read two ways. A tight quote costs ten minutes and saves weeks of argument.

How Quotation works in practice

State clearly whether prices are inclusive or exclusive of GST, give the quote a number and a validity date, and carry the accepted quotation through to the invoice unchanged so the customer sees the same figures twice.

faq.question: Is a quotation legally binding?
faq.answer: Generally it is an offer rather than a contract, and binding once accepted within its validity period on the stated terms.

faq.question: Should a quotation show GST?
faq.answer: Yes. Showing the tax separately removes the single most common misunderstanding about the final payable amount.
